'''Hans-Ulrich Reissig''' ({{langx|de|link=no|Hans-Ulrich Reißig}}; born 9 May 1949) is a German chemist and was a full professor of [[Organic Chemistry]] at [[FU Berlin]].<ref name="Fachbereich Biologie, Chemie, Pharmazie 2020">{{cite web | title=Prof. Dr. Hans-Ulrich Reissig | website=fu-berlin.de: Fachbereich Biologie, Chemie, Pharmazie | date=15 September 2020 | url=https://www.bcp.fu-berlin.de/en/chemie/chemie/forschung/OrgChem/reissig/Prof_Dr_Hans-Ulrich_Reissig/index.html | access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref>

== Education and academic career ==
Reissig was born in [[Helmbrechts]], Bavaria, Germany. He studied chemistry at [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]] (Germany) from 1970 to 1975, where he completed his PhD in 1978 under the supervision of [[Rolf Huisgen]], with a thesis "Neue Beiträge zu den Additionen der Diazoalkane und zur Chemie der 3H-Pyrazole"  (Contributions to the Additions of Diazoalkanes and the Chemistry of 3H-Pyrazoles).<ref>{{OCLC|251406584}}</ref> After a postdoctoral research stay at [[University of British Columbia]], Vancouver, with Edward Piers (1938–2010), he started his independent research at the [[Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg]] (Germany) in 1979 under the mentorship of Siegfried Hünig finishing his habilitation in 1984 (Chemistry of Donor-Acceptor Cyclopropanes). As Heisenberg awardee and lecturer he stayed in [[Würzburg]] until 1986. From 1986 to 1993, he was associate professor at [[TU Darmstadt]] and after the German reunification full professor at [[TU Dresden]] from 1993 to 1999.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://tu-dresden.de/tu-dresden/newsportal/ressourcen/dateien/universitaetsjournal/uj_pdfs/uj_1995/UJ09-95.pdf |title=Prof. Dr. rer. nat. habil. Hans-Ulrich Reißig |last= |first= |date=1995 |website=tu-dresden.de |publisher=TU Dresden |page=5 |access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref> He was professor at [[FU Berlin]] from 1999 to his retirement in 2015.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bertelsmann |first=C. |date=11 November 2015 |title=Experimentierfreude |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/karriere/professor-fuer-organische-chemie-experimentierfreude-1.2730166 |work=[[Süddeutsche Zeitung]] |location=Munich |language=de |access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref>

== Research contributions==
His research interests include the development of new synthetic methods, the investigation of reaction mechanisms and the synthesis of natural products. In 1980 he introduced the term "Donor-Acceptor Substituted Cyclopropanes" and used these building blocks systematically in his research. He is particularly interested in reactions of lithiated alkoxyallenes, the use of samarium diiodide in synthesis and cycloadditions of nitroso alkenes. Besides the synthesis of a broad range of heterocycles his group achieved total syntheses of natural products (strychnine, γ-rubromycin etc.) as well as the syntheses of bioactive compounds such as carbohydrate mimetics.

==Honors ==
Reissig was awarded the Karl-Winnacker Fellowship of the Hoechst AG in 1985. He has been a corresponding member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities since 2012 and received the [[Liebig Medal]] of the Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker in 2014.<ref name="Freie Universität Berlin 2020">{{cite web | title=Chemiker Prof. Dr. Hans-Ulrich Reißig geehrt | website=Freie Universität Berlin | date=7 August 2014 | url=https://www.fu-berlin.de/presse/informationen/fup/2014/fup_14_284-gdch-ehrt-professor-reissig/index.html | language=de | access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref>
